doc.title: Iola Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, CT, July 17, 2011

title: Jazz's place in public culture and audiences
summary: Why jazz is absent from TV, the need for school education, and more young audiences in Europe.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: And why is that? I mean you don’t see jazz on television.
Unless it’s a special event. But that is true. And I guess it’s a double-edged sword. Jazz is a highly respected art form.

Yeah. Now it’s a respected art so it seems whoever is in charge of things seems to think okay it’s not for the general public. And I don’t think that’s true. I think given an opportunity that the public would go for jazz. If given an opportunity through radio, television, and just part of our everyday commercial life, if it was there I think it would be accepted and enjoyed. It takes perhaps a little more educated ear and that’s been one of my hobby horses, education in the schools. Because it has to start from there. And that’s why I think you find young people in general, this is a big generality, in Europe accepting jazz as just one more form of music while at the same time they go for the pop stuff and rock and all of that, but they also accept jazz much more I think than in this country, the young people who have not been exposed to jazz and don’t really know about it just seem to think it’s something that’s way over there.
It’s curious because we invented jazz in America, right?
And unfortunately sometimes things seem worthwhile if they come from somewhere else. We think they’re exotic.

I really don’t know just what it is, but in the years that Dave has toured in Europe, just looking at the audience you can see a lot more younger people in the audiences in Europe than you’d see here. Not to say that there aren’t some here, but just more young people really interested in jazz. I think it’s just part of their culture and part of their education to have some understanding of all the genres of music.
There’s many, many young people who love jazz but they want to be the players, right? I thing we need more in the audience. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-
Yes. There are many people who want to play but they need to have an audience and there is the rub.
